For the Track 2 theme of Aerial Surveillance and Rapid Delivery; the primary design
driver the ability combine   vertical   take-offllanding   flexibility  (no runway
dependency; precision hover over a delivery point) with the range and endurance of
fixed-wing cruise flight:  This directly motivated hybrid VTOL configuration rather
than pure multirotor pure   fixed-wing   platform: The   development process
followed a requirements-first approach: mission profile and payload constraints were
fixed  first (4 kg MTOW, 20 km range, 250 payload) , after which  propulsion,
structure, and avionics were iteratively sized around those constraints_
The design philosophy adopted for this platform prioritizes decoupled subsystems
over sharedlmulti-role hardware. This decision was made early in the concept phase
after evaluating common failure modes in hybrid VTOL platforms where combined
liftlcruise propulsion (tilt-rotor;   tail-sitter)   architectures tend to  introduce control
complexity that is disproportionate to the performance gained relative to a decoupled
lift-plus-cruise layout: In  tilt-rotor   designs, the same   propulsion units must be
actuated   through mechanical tilt   mechanism and re-tuned across both  flight
regimes while tail-sitters   require the entire airframe to pitch through 90" during
transition, placing high demands on attitude estimation and control-law robustness at
low airspeed: A dedicated lift-rotor and pusher-motor arrangement avoids both of
these failure-prone mechanisms_ allowing each propulsion subsystem to be sized,
tuned, and validated independently against its own flight regime.

piovde] The quad-plane hybrid VTOL (four dedicated lift rotors one pusher cruise
motor) was selected as decouples the lift and cruise propulsion   systems,
simplifying control law design compared to tilt-rotor or tail-sitter architectures, at the
cost of carrying dead weight (lift motors) during cruise an accepted trade-off given
the team's fabrication and avionics tuning timeline_
The airframe uses mid-mounted, 1.5 m span fixed wing as the primary lifting
surface during cruise_ Four  VTOL lift   motors (10"  propellers) are  mounted on
symmetric booms extending from the wing; positioned   fore   and   shaft of   the
estimated CG to provide pitch and roll control authority during hover: A single pusher
motor (12" propeller) is mounted at the rear of the 700 mm fuselage for forward
thrust  during   cruise and  transition_ The  payload bay is located at the fuselage
underside, close to the estimated CG, so that payload release does not produce a
significant pitching moment: The flight controller; GPS, ad telemetry are housed
centrally in the fuselage for short wiring runs and to keep mass concentrated near
the CG
